title: Cannabis Mimosa Bar with Citrus and THC Tinctures
h1: A Self-Serve Citrus Mimosa Bar with THC Tinctures
metaDescription: Build a self-serve cannabis mimosa bar on sparkling water or alcohol-free bubbles, with citrus juices and labeled tinctures that guests measure themselves.
excerpt: Juices on ice, alcohol-free bubbles and labeled tincture bottles with dose cards: a brunch bar where every guest builds and doses their own glass.
keyTakeaways: Each guest builds their own glass: juice, bubbles, garnish and, if they choose, one measured tincture dose.
Label every bottle with its mg per ml, give each its own dropper, and post a card that says start low and wait 2 hours.

body:
A cannabis mimosa bar turns brunch into a build-your-own station: chilled juices, sparkling water or alcohol-free bubbles, citrus garnishes and labeled THC or CBD tinctures. Every guest pours, mixes and doses their own glass, so nobody drinks an amount someone else picked.

## The tincture station

- Label each bottle with the cannabinoid (THC or CBD) and its mg per ml, taken from the product label.
- Give every bottle its own dropper or measuring syringe, and never swap them between bottles.
- Post a card: start low, take one measured dose, then wait 2 hours.
- Leave alcohol out. The CDC notes that using alcohol and cannabis together is likely to impair you more than either alone.

New to tinctures? Our [cannabis tincture guide](/blog/cannabis-tincture-guide/) covers how they work, and our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/) helps with a starting amount.

## Juices, bubbles and garnishes

Set out three or four chilled juices, such as orange, grapefruit, blood orange and tangerine, beside chilled sparkling water or alcohol-free sparkling wine. Add citrus wheels and twists for garnish. Shopping for a tincture? Check your nearest High Society store's [online menu](/shop/) first, since selection varies by store, and a budtender can walk you through the label.

## How to pour a cannabis mimosa

Pour about one part juice to three parts bubbles into a flute. Add a measured tincture dose if you'd like a THC mimosa, then stir gently: THC doesn't dissolve in water, so a quick stir helps spread it through the glass. For more mixing ideas, see our guide to [making cannabis-infused drinks](/blog/how-to-make-cannabis-infused-cocktails/).

## Matching citrus to a tincture's aroma notes

A single-strain tincture comes from one named cultivar's extract instead of a blend, and some labels describe its aroma. If a tincture leans citrusy, which often points to [limonene](/blog/limonene-terpene/), the terpene behind much of citrus peel's scent, an orange or grapefruit juice echoes it. Think of it as a flavor game: aroma notes tell you about taste, not about how a glass will feel.

## When the party wraps

Mixed drinks aren't saved, so pour out anything left in glasses. Tinctures go back into their labeled bottles and up high, away from children and pets. If someone swallows a tincture by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222.

Want food that works the same way? Pair the bar with our [build-your-own avocado toast](/blog/choose-your-own-adventure-avocado-toast-brunch/). 21+ only. Please consume responsibly.

faq.q: How many drops of tincture go in a mimosa?
faq.a: Measure in milliliters rather than drops, because drop size varies. Check the label's mg per ml: 0.5 ml of a tincture labeled 5 mg per ml is about 2.5 mg. Health Canada suggests new consumers start at 2.5 mg of THC or less. Drink one glass, then wait at least 2 hours.

faq.q: Can I mix THC with champagne?
faq.a: We don't recommend it. Alcohol and THC together are likely to impair you more than either alone. In a controlled driving-simulator study, people who combined edibles and alcohol often drove worse than with either one by itself. If some guests want real sparkling wine, keep those glasses tincture-free.

faq.q: How do I keep guests from overdoing it?
faq.a: Build the limits into the setup. Use labeled bottles with measured droppers and a card that says one dose, then wait 2 hours. Keep plenty of zero-THC bubbles and food out, with no alcohol on the infused side of the bar. Close the tincture station after the first round, and make sure nobody who doses drives.

ingredients: 2 bottles (750 ml each) alcohol-free sparkling wine, well chilled, or 1.5 liters sparkling water
3 or 4 citrus juices, about 1 cup each: orange, grapefruit, blood orange or tangerine
Orange, lemon and grapefruit wheels and twists
THC and/or CBD tinctures in labeled bottles, each with its own dropper or syringe
Dose cards and a start-low card
A tub of ice for the juice carafes
steps: Chill the bubbles and juices thoroughly, then nest the juice carafes in a tub of ice.
Arrange the tinctures, their droppers and the dose cards on their own tray, apart from the juices.
Pour about 1 1/2 ounces of juice into a flute and top with about 4 1/2 ounces of bubbles.
Add one measured tincture dose if you like, and stir gently to spread it through the drink.
Finish with a citrus wheel or twist and serve right away.
After the party, cap the tinctures and put them away, and pour out any mixed drinks left in glasses.
recipe.dosingNote: **Per-glass math:** ml of tincture × the label's mg per ml = THC in the glass. Example: 0.5 ml of a tincture labeled 5 mg per ml is about 2.5 mg. A homemade tincture is an estimate that depends on the starting flower's potency and on decarboxylation and extraction losses. Start low, wait at least 2 hours before another infused glass, keep every bottle labeled, and keep tinctures away from children and pets.

sources.label: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention: Cannabis frequently asked questions
Zamarripa C.A. et al. (2026), Impact of cannabis edibles combined with alcohol on driving, JAMA Network Open
Health Canada: What you need to know if you choose to consume cannabis
PubChem (U.S. National Library of Medicine): Tetrahydrocannabinol, solubility

review.summary: 16 claims checked: 15 ok, 1 overstated (1 fixed). Alcohol stays out of the infused side; no terpene or mood claim.

claims.claim: Using alcohol and cannabis together is likely to impair you more than either alone (body, takeaway, FAQ)
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html (WebFetch): 'Using alcohol and cannabis at the same time is likely to result in greater impairment than when using either one alone.'

claims.claim: In a controlled study, people who combined edibles and alcohol often drove worse than with either one alone
claims.fix: now 'a controlled driving-simulator study': the trial measured simulated driving, not road driving; the 'often' finding itself is as stated
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13135220/ (Zamarripa 2026, JAMA Netw Open, abstract via E-utilities, PMID 42065887): objective 'simulated driving'; 'Driving impairment and subjective intoxication (eg, confidence to drive) were often greater under co-use conditions compared with cannabis or alcohol alone.'

claims.claim: Health Canada suggests new consumers start at 2.5 mg of THC or less
claims.source: https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-medication/cannabis/resources/what-you-need-to-know-if-you-choose-to-consume-cannabis.html (WebFetch): 'if you are a new consumer, look for a product containing 2.5 mg of THC or less.'

claims.claim: Tincture math: ml × label mg per ml; 0.5 ml of a 5 mg/ml tincture is about 2.5 mg
Measure in milliliters rather than drops, because drop size varies
claims.source: general measuring practice (a drop's volume depends on the dropper and the liquid); cautious instruction, no figure

claims.claim: THC doesn't dissolve in water, so a quick stir helps spread it through the glass
claims.source: https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/16078 (PUG View Solubility via the PubChem REST API): 'Essentially insoluble in water'; the text says stirring spreads it, not that it dissolves

claims.claim: Wait at least 2 hours before another infused glass; start low
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html: 'it can take up to 2 hours to feel the effects from the drug.'

claims.claim: A homemade tincture is an estimate that depends on flower potency and decarboxylation and extraction losses
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/ (Wang 2016, full text via Europe PMC REST): 'the conversion of the acid to Δ9-THC was never perfectly complete without loss or degradation of starting material'

claims.claim: A citrusy tincture often points to limonene, the terpene behind much of citrus peel's scent; aroma notes tell you about taste, not how a glass will feel
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7321087/ (Ibáñez 2020, Molecules, abstract via E-utilities, PMID 32503168): title 'Encapsulated Limonene: A Pleasant Lemon-Like Aroma ...'; 'Limonene, mainly found as a major component in Citrus spp.'; no effect claim made (brief mustAvoid)

claims.claim: A single-strain tincture comes from one named cultivar's extract instead of a blend
claims.source: definition of the term as used on product labels; no figure or effect attached

claims.claim: Pour about one part juice to three parts bubbles (1 1/2 oz juice, 4 1/2 oz bubbles); 1.5 liters of bubbles for 8 glasses
claims.source: arithmetic: 1.5 : 4.5 = 1 : 3; 8 × 4.5 oz = 36 oz, about 1.06 liters, under the 1.5 liters listed

claims.claim: Tinctures go back in labeled bottles, up high, away from children and pets; pour out mixed drinks
claims.source: Health Canada page above: store edible cannabis 'securely' and 'out of reach of children, youth, and pets.'

claims.claim: If someone swallows a tincture by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html: 'call a poison control center at: at 1-800-222-1222.'

claims.claim: Make sure nobody who doses drives
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-au-impaired-driving (Michigan bans driving while under the influence)

claims.claim: High Society: check your nearest store's online menu first, since selection varies by store, and a budtender can walk you through the label
claims.source: facts/hs-facts.json services.productCategories (tinctures on the Birch Run and New Buffalo menus), services.inStoreVisit ('a budtender ... helps you choose'), compliance.responsibleUseLines ('Selection varies—check today's availability.'); no product named as stocked

review.notes: Independent fact-check, 2026-10-24. The CDC FAQ and Health Canada reopened with WebFetch; the Zamarripa 2026 and Ibáñez 2020 abstracts read through NCBI E-utilities; THC solubility from PubChem's REST API. Sparkling wine appears only with the impairment caution, as the brief asks. Sources list kept: all four are https and support the text as now worded. High Society: one mention (online menu, selection varies, budtender help), in hs-facts. Writer's notes: Alcohol-free by default; sparkling wine mentioned only with the impairment caution (brief angle). No terpene-mood claims. High Society mentioned once (menu; selection varies; budtender helps read labels).
